title: Expiration Odometer of a Moved Kessler Care Fleet 12-Visit Plan
content:
**Formula clause.** When a Kessler Care Fleet 12-Visit plan of the Kessler Care Prepaid Maintenance Plans is moved, its new expiration odometer is the replacement unit's starting reading plus the miles left on the plan, in whole miles. The replacement unit is the unit delivered on the customer's single Kessler Fleet Vehicle Purchase Agreement standing in closed status.
- **Miles left** are the plan's expiration odometer less the retired unit's closing reading, never below 0.
- **Retired unit's closing reading** is the plan's last recorded visit reading. That is the highest odometer on the plan's redemption entries, whether reinstated or not; where the odometer at sale is higher, or there is no such entry, it is the odometer at sale.
- **Replacement unit's starting reading** is its odometer at delivery on that agreement.

Mileage allowances that apply are added to that sum.

## Worked figures (hypothetical)
| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Plan's expiration odometer before the move | 95,000 |
| Highest odometer on the plan's redemption entries | 58,200 (above the odometer at sale of 4,100) |
| Closing reading | 58,200 |
| Miles left | 95,000 less 58,200, which is 36,800 |
| Replacement odometer at delivery | 120 |
| New expiration odometer | 36,920 |

If the plan had no redemption entry, the closing reading would be the odometer at sale of 4,100, and the miles left would be 90,900. If the closing reading were above the plan's expiration odometer, the miles left would be 0, and the new expiration odometer would equal the starting reading. A hypothetical allowance of 500 miles that applies is added to the sum, giving 37,420 in the main example.
